variants.text:
By now this probably sounds terribly artificial. Is anyone actually going to do scheduled check-ins, delayed cohabitation, conversations about hypothetical disasters, imagination exercises, not to mention resisting the heat of the moment stuff, and continuing your own reparenting practices when a warm body is available to do some of the soothing?

Well, you caught me. It is painfully artificial.

That’s part of why. I’m trying to replace a missing community with instructions. Build the community and you can probably throw some of the instructions away.

## What doing it consciously looks like

Most of this I learned by screwing it up. Some I figured out by thinking. A few parts I’m still testing.

Say I meet somebody tomorrow and we both get excited. Before making love, I’d want to talk about jealousy, attraction to other people, what happens when one of us is stressed, old patterns, how recent the healing is, what we want from each other in a hard moment, and money. But I don’t want to spend three days interviewing her either. Some of that I’d put into scenarios: “If X happened, what would you want and what would you probably do?” If we can only give each other abstract answers, usually we don’t know yet. Then go do normal things. Ten profound conversations in one weekend can feel deep before there’s much relationship there to be deep.

If sex happens, I don’t want it to automatically answer the housing question. If housing makes separate living difficult, fine, but once we live together, practical necessity starts narrowing choices. I’d put an actual check-in date on the calendar before there’s a crisis.

Meanwhile I’d want us to make friends together. My old friends will be partial to me and hers to her. Fine. I just don’t want two separate camps to be the only people who know us.

I also need to remember that wanting her romantically and wanting to build my life with her are different decisions. She can be a wonderful lover and a terrible co-parent, community member, or life partner. “I’m taking a chance on her” can turn into “she’s the right person” without me noticing I changed the claim. That second claim needs more time.

And I keep my inner practices. Being loved doesn’t mean I’m done learning to love or regulate myself. If some part of me says, Wait. Slow down. Something doesn’t fit. I need to ask this, I stop and ask it. I don’t want chemistry answering on my behalf.

# If you’re already in it

If you’re already married, living together, raising children, or ten years in, you can’t use the part about slowing down before the relationship has momentum. It already has momentum.

I wish I had a special method for this part. I don’t. In all three of my reference relationships I could keep bringing up the same problem, but I couldn’t make the other person look at it with me. One person can’t create mutual honesty. It’s probably common sense; I still had to learn it.

With Bee and Key, the biggest thing sitting underneath everything was trust. They wanted to be with me and would say they trusted me, but really they didn’t trust me, themself, or anyone else. It was all or nothing: blind trust, or none.
